xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-4400: One-click provider presets: "Apply Anthropic defaults" / "Apply OpenAI defaults", backed by eval results and documented

plan.title: One-click provider presets: "Apply Anthropic defaults" / "Apply OpenAI defaults", backed by eval results and documented
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

metadata.sizeJustification: The finalize surface lint counts every Mintlify page, fixture and generated manifest as its own two-segment subsystem, so any slice that carries its required docs and CLI lockstep files (pan-help fixture, slash-command manifest, synced-skills fixture) exceeds 6 subsystems; a sibling split would not avoid this. Issue AC3 also requires the CLI and the Settings UI to render one diff engine, so the lib, CLI and UI slices ship together. The work is already decomposed into 9 items with a narrow DAG.

narratives.Problem: Operators must set about 40 model and effort settings by hand to get a coherent single-provider lineup. The eval evidence (docs/model-evals/2026-09-29-opus-5-5-vs-sonnet-5-5.md) and the GPT-6 routing research exist, but nothing applies them in one step, and the existing whole-document settings save rewrites roles wholesale, writes env API keys in plaintext and drops sub-keys, so it cannot apply a preset without touching unrelated config.
narratives.Proposal: Versioned preset data in src/lib/model-presets/presets.ts (anthropic, anthropic-cost-saver pilot, openai) covers a registry of every model and effort config path with a value or an explicit keep plus reason. A read-only plan engine computes a per-setting diff with a credential gate and canUseHarness checks. A path-scoped config.yaml write (parseDocument + setIn/deleteIn, validation through mergeConfigs, compare-and-swap, atomic rename) applies it inside runSettingsWriteSerialized and records a single-level undo and lastApplied in ~/.overdeck/model-presets-state.json. Four HTTP routes, `pan models preset list|show|apply|undo`, and Settings > Model Routing buttons with a diff dialog, an Undo toast and a 'preset updated' notice all render the same plan object. A user page, configuration/model-presets.mdx, documents each placement with its eval evidence.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No Google/Gemini preset
- No change to product defaults (DEFAULT_WORKHORSES.expensive claude-opus-4-8, the flywheel literal in src/lib/config-yaml/roles.ts)
- No deletion or rewiring of GET /api/settings/optimal-defaults or /minimax-defaults
- No change to providers.ts tierModels, the capability class table, or Codex version floors
- No auto-apply of a newer preset version
- No multi-level undo or preset history
- No fix to saveSettingsApi's plaintext key write-back or dropped sub-keys (separate issue)
- No enabling of tiered execution, and no creation of tiers or a supervisor
- No persistence of preset state in config.yaml (the retired models.preset key stays retired)
- No routes added to src/dashboard/server/routes/settings.ts and no scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt raise
- No Claude Code subagent model setting (none exists; subagents inherit the session model)
- No use of saveSettingsApi or writeYamlConfigPreservingComments for preset writes

autoDecisions.summary: Apply presets through a new path-scoped YAML write, not saveSettingsApi
autoDecisions.rationale: saveSettingsApi rewrites workhorses/roles wholesale (settings-api.ts:785-786), writes env-derived API keys back in plaintext (:946-958), drops tts.summarizer.batch_window_seconds and memory.features.knowledge_index, and copies project .pan.yaml values into the global file; issue AC1 cannot hold on that path. The new door still uses runSettingsWriteSerialized.

autoDecisions.summary: The AC1 test fixture uses $VAR env references and literal keys instead of 'masked keys'
autoDecisions.rationale: Overdeck has no server-side API-key masking; the closest real risk is env references and project-only values leaking into config.yaml.

autoDecisions.summary: The CLI writes through the lib directly, with a compare-and-swap on config.yaml text for cross-process safety
autoDecisions.rationale: This matches how pan skills writes config; the per-process queue cannot serialize a CLI and the dashboard, so a re-read before write aborts on a concurrent change.

autoDecisions.summary: Ship three presets: anthropic, anthropic-cost-saver (pilot), openai
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator's issue comment allows the cost-saver variant, and it is two data rows on top of anthropic, clearly labelled pilot.

autoDecisions.summary: Ship the OpenAI preset now with evidence.status 'research'
autoDecisions.rationale: The operator asked for the OpenAI button and AC3 exercises it; no GPT eval exists yet (the 2026-09-29 run used a Claude-only route), so the docs state that plainly per placement.

autoDecisions.summary: The OpenAI preset keeps background AI models (titles, compaction, fork summary, handoff author, status review, TTS summarizer, memory extraction, provider fallback)
autoDecisions.rationale: Background AI runs through `claude -p` (transcript-summary.ts:344), so an OpenAI model would need the CLIProxy route; the research rates GPT-6 Luna 'not yet' for summaries and memory (77% hallucination); the 272K GPT pin excludes the 1M fork-summary slot. They are reported as 'not set' rows.

autoDecisions.summary: Missing credentials block the whole preset; a harness-policy denial skips only that row, except a denied workhorse row, which blocks
autoDecisions.rationale: 'requires that provider's credentials/harness to be available, and says what it could not set'; roles reference workhorse slots, so a partial workhorse write would be incoherent.

autoDecisions.summary: Tier rows are computed from existing tiers by hardest difficulty; an existing distribution is removed; tiered_execution.enabled and tier creation are never touched
autoDecisions.rationale: Tier names are user-defined and the default is tiers: {}; a preset fills explicit settings only and must not change whether tiered execution runs.

autoDecisions.summary: Anthropic tier band complex/expert uses workhorse:expensive (Opus 5.5), not Fable 5.1
autoDecisions.rationale: No eval covers Fable 5.1, and it costs 2.5x Opus 5.5; a later preset version can add it.

autoDecisions.summary: Review lanes are set to parent under roles.review.model = workhorse:expensive in every preset
autoDecisions.rationale: The eval keeps review on Opus; parent makes all four lanes follow the review model, as the eval report's recommended config describes.

autoDecisions.summary: Undo is single-level and restores only paths still holding the preset's value
autoDecisions.rationale: This restores previous values exactly (AC2) without clobbering edits the operator made after the apply.

autoDecisions.summary: Preset state (lastApplied, undo record) lives in ~/.overdeck/model-presets-state.json, not config.yaml
autoDecisions.rationale: The models.preset YAML key is retired (docs/CONFIGURATION.md:248); prior values and the applied version cannot be derived, so a small state file is legitimate.

autoDecisions.summary: Add `pan models preset undo` beside the issue's list/show/apply
autoDecisions.rationale: Undo must be reachable where the CLI apply happens; it reuses the same lib function as the UI Undo.

autoDecisions.summary: Settings page replaces formData after a preset apply or undo
autoDecisions.rationale: The page's whole-document autosave refreshes only workhorses/roles/ui/part of conversations, so a stale formData would revert preset-written paths on the next unrelated edit.

autoDecisions.summary: Keep one issue with sizeJustification instead of sibling issues
autoDecisions.rationale: The surface lint counts each doc page and fixture as a subsystem, so any docs-carrying slice trips it; AC3 needs CLI and UI on one diff engine.
The TTS summarizer posts to https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions with apiKeys.openai (tts-summarizer.ts:114), so a Claude id breaks it and an OpenAI id needs an API key plus the E4 gate.
